name: Capability Surface Reconciliation
summary: Build a dated inventory of advertised skills and tools, then reconcile discovery, connection, execution and publication claims against their actual evidence.
problem: A handover or published listing can imply that a tool integration works even when only skills, metadata or an unpublished discovery draft have been verified.
coreOutcomes: Complete paginated skill and tool metadata inventory
Distinct-name counts with provider surfaces preserved
Separate capability, authority and runtime evidence axes
Contradiction handling bound to version, target and time
Procedure-to-product mapping without republishing external implementations
requirements: Authorised prior work evidence and current repository decisions
Access to the current skill catalogues and tool registry
Account-specific or runtime readback when those claims need verification
A public/private publication boundary for saved metadata
boundaries: Advertised capabilities are not proof of connection or successful execution
Inventorying a tool does not authorise its use
External platform skills and tools are dependencies, not owned products
Does not enumerate unconnected remote servers or lifetime invocations
Does not change the shop's CLI-first interface
